content.title: Gov't shutdown could have lasting effects on airlines. Here's why.
content.description:
The airline industry could see long-term impacts from the government shutdown, Raymond James managing director Savi Syth tells Yahoo Finance. Syth explains that while the government is shut down, there isn't air traffic controller training, another headwind for a workforce that is already in short supply.

Also catch what Hickory Global Partners president Chris Dane has to say about shutdown pressures airline operators could be faced with, all this coming after Delta Air Lines (DAL) topped third quarter earnings estimates.

To watch more expert insights and analysis on the latest market action, check out more Market Domination.

content.title: What could push airlines to tipping point if US shutdown drags on

Delta Air Lines (DAL) stock is lifting off on Thursday after topping third quarter estimates: revenue of $15.2 billion (vs. estimates of $15.1 billion) and adjusted earnings of $1.71 per share (vs. estimates of $1.56). As the US government's shutdown moves into its ninth day, what sort of disruptions could airline operators see in the coming days if the shutdown drags on longer?

content.title: Spirit Airlines to furlough 1,800 flight attendants amid second bankruptcy
content.summary: Spirit Airlines plans to furlough 1,800 flight attendants before the end of the year, the cash-strapped budget carrier said Monday.  The company said it made the “difficult decision” to put cabin crew members on temporary leave to match staffing needs with expected flight demand during Spirit's second bankruptcy in a year.  Spirit filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection last month and subsequently announced that it planned to suspend operations in about a dozen U.S. cities beginning in October.
